description: Stereo feedback delay network reverb with separate decay times for the low and mid bands, high-frequency damping, a pre-delay and a modulated tail

params.text: Passes the signal through the reverb when on; with it off the module is bypassed
Sets how long the low band takes to fall 60dB, 0.5 seconds fully counter-clockwise to 32 seconds fully clockwise
Sets how long the mid band takes to fall 60dB, 0.5 seconds fully counter-clockwise to 32 seconds fully clockwise
Sets the frequency dividing the low band from the mid band, 50Hz to 1000Hz
Sets the frequency at which the decay time has fallen to half the MID time, 1.5kHz to 22kHz, so turning it down shortens the top of the tail
Delays the reverb behind the dry signal by 0 to 250ms, which makes the space read as a larger one
Sets how far the modulation moves the decay times, 0 to 100%, from a static tail to a wavering one
Sets the rate of the LFO that modulates the decay times, 0.5Hz to 20Hz
Sets how much reverb is in the output, 0 to 100% wet

inputs.text: Adds to the LOW time knob, where 10V covers the whole of that knob's travel
Adds to the MID time knob, where 10V covers the whole of that knob's travel
Adds to the DAMP knob, where 10V covers the whole of that knob's travel
Adds to the DELAY knob, where 10V covers the whole of that knob's travel
Adds to the MIX knob, where 10V covers the whole of that knob's travel
The left audio input into the reverb
The right audio input into the reverb

outputs.text: The left output, carrying the dry signal and the reverb in the proportion set by MIX
The right output, carrying the dry signal and the reverb in the proportion set by MIX

notes: the reverb algorithm runs at 44100Hz whatever the patch's sample rate, and the module resamples into and out of it
X-OVER, M.RATE and M.AMT have no input jack, so those three take no voltage control
